t2i_prompt: Flat UI mockup, no device frame, of a <CONTENT> section drawn as an engineering drawing sheet. Deep navy background, off-white 1 px linework, one steel-blue accent for numbers and short underline rules. A double-line sheet border with zone numbers along the top and bottom and letters down the sides, centring arrows at the midpoints, and a title block in the bottom-right corner with labelled cells for revision, scale and drawing number. Content set in numbered columns separated by thin vertical rules. A narrow phone version beside it with the same border and accordion rows. Mono caps labels, square corners, no shadows, calm generous spacing.
signature_idea: The site's footer is the border of an engineering drawing, ending every page with a zone frame and a title block that carries revision and drawing number.
strengths: memorable, ownable closer that speaks directly to engineers
title block gives a natural home for legal, revision and contact data
navy ground plus steel-blue accent is exactly on palette
weaknesses: title block filled with nonsense labels shows it can read as pastiche if not edited
zone letters and ticks add noise for non-engineering readers
condensed link text is less refined than Geist light
brand_fit_why: Navy ground, off-white lines, a single steel-blue accent, mono figures and square corners match the brand book closely; it became the shipped Footer.
